title: SIU clears officer in fatal shooting: Fred Kirkey died by his own gun
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has determined that the Ontario Provincial Police were not responsible for the death of a gunman who shot himself in the chest during a confrontation with police near Prescott in July.
An autopsy determined that Fred Kirkey was wounded by two bullets, one from a police handgun and the other from his own rifle. He died from massive blood loss caused by the rifle bullet.
The incident occurred after OPP arrived at a house on County Road 26 in Maynard on July 23.
Mr. Maynard, who was to start serving a five-month jail sentence for impaired driving on the day he died, had told his friends he would rather die than return to jail.
An eyewitness said Mr. Maynard crashed his car into the back of a vehicle belonging to the boyfriend of his estranged wife.
When police arrived they pleaded with him to put his gun down. Mr. Kirkey fired at police instead. Police returned fire.
Mr. Kirkey was already prohibited from owning a gun after an incident in which he emptied the bullets from a gun in the parking lot of an area Burger King.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that have resulted in serious injury, sexual assault or death.
